title: Fertilizer for Rice: A Season Plan for Irrigated and Rainfed Palay
metaTitle: Fertilizer for Rice: Season Plan, Timing and Computation
metaDescription: Fertilizer for rice made simple: basal and top dressing by days after transplanting, PhilRice bag plans, a sample computation, and tips for rainfed palay.
excerpt: The right fertilizer for rice depends on your soil, your variety and your season, but the plan always follows the same growth stages. This guide lays out a full palay season based on PhilRice recommendations. It covers the basal dose, when to top dress, how to compute the bags, and how rainfed fields differ from irrigated ones.

blocks.text:
Fertilizer is money you bury in the mud, so it has to work. PhilRice found that in 2020, fertilizer took about 8 percent of the total cost of producing rice. Seeds and pesticides took only 3 to 4 percent each.

PhilRice teaches the method through its PalayCheck System, which many farmers search as the palay check system. Key Check 5 asks for enough nutrients from tillering to early panicle initiation and flowering. At dough stage, aim for at least 300 panicles per square meter in transplanted rice, or 350 in direct seeded rice.
Why fertilizer is important for palay

Every harvest carries nutrients out of your field. IRRI counts what the crop takes up for each ton of grain. That is about 16 kg of nitrogen, 6.4 kg of phosphate and 19 kg of potash. So a 5 ton harvest takes up about 80 kg of nitrogen, 32 kg of phosphate and 95 kg of potash. Fertilizer fills the gap between that need and what the soil, water and straw supply.

Many farmers leave part of that gap open. A PhilRice survey of irrigated farms in 2016 and 2017 found far less phosphorus and potassium than recommended. Short feeding means slow growth, fewer tillers and panicles, and lighter grain. Too much nitrogen is also bad, because it invites lodging and pests.
Start with a soil test, MOET or the Rice Crop Manager
Before you buy, find out what your soil lacks. PalayCheck lists these tools.

items: **Soil analysis** at a soils laboratory. Ask your municipal agriculturist where to send samples.
**MOET**, the Minus One Element Technique: rice grown in pots of your own soil, each pot missing one nutrient. An app turns the result into fertilizer amounts.
**Leaf color chart**, a four color ruler that shows when the crop needs nitrogen.
**Rice Crop Manager**, an online tool from IRRI and the DA that gives a fertilizer guideline for your field.

blocks.text: No tool at hand? Use the PhilRice general recommendation as a guide. For irrigated lowland rice, it lists 97 kg of nitrogen per hectare in the wet season. In the dry season it lists 139 kg. A quarter of the nitrogen goes on at 7 to 14 days after transplanting (DAT). Another quarter goes at mid tillering, and half at maximum tillering or early panicle initiation. All the phosphorus goes on first. Potassium goes 70 percent at 7 to 14 DAT and 30 percent around panicle initiation.
A season plan of fertilizer for rice, by days after transplanting

PhilRice turned those rules into bags per hectare for its Abonong Swak campaign. Below is its plan for a target of 5 to 6 tons per hectare. Check the days to harvest on your seed bag, because the dates follow variety maturity.

blocks.caption: PhilRice Abonong Swak plan per hectare for 5 to 6 tons. DAS in brackets is for direct seeded rice. Adjust it to your soil test.
rows: Second top dressing: 1 bag urea and half a bag 0 0 60

blocks.text:
The plan also works organic matter into the field. It uses 5 to 6 tons of rice straw. At 14 DAT, it adds 10 bags of decomposed chicken manure, commercial organic fertilizer or vermicompost. In the seedbed, it adds a little zinc sulfate and 14 14 14.

For a 3 to 4 ton target, PhilRice uses 1 bag of 14 14 14 at basal. Later comes 1 bag of urea with half a bag of 0 0 60. For 7 to 8 tons, it doubles the urea to 2 bags at each top dressing. Our guides to [pagtatanim ng palay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay) and [palay](/crops/palay) cover the rest of the crop.
What each bag does

items: [Complete fertilizer 14 14 14](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14) or [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer) at basal gives early phosphorus for the roots.
[Urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), the usual fertilizer for top dressing, feeds tillers and panicles.
[Potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer) near panicle initiation helps fill the grain and keeps stems standing.
[Ammonium sulfate](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), the 21 0 0 fertilizer, can replace urea where soil lacks sulfur, at about 2.2 bags per bag of urea.

blocks.title: Let the leaves decide the last nitrogen
blocks.text: Own a leaf color chart? Read it every 7 days from 14 DAT, or 21 DAS, until early flowering. Apply nitrogen when 6 or more of 10 leaves read below 4. For direct seeded rice, the cutoff is 3.5.
Irrigated and rainfed palay

Irrigated fields yield more in the dry season, and the PhilRice general recommendation feeds them more. It gives 139 kg of nitrogen in the dry season against 97 kg in the wet. Where the sun is strong, like Nueva Ecija, Bicol and Isabela, PhilRice also adds muriate of potash around panicle initiation. That raises grain size and weight.

Rainfed fields go through the same stages on a different rhythm. Fertilizer needs moisture to reach the roots, so time each dose to a wet field, not a fixed date. IRRI says broadcast direct seeded rice can take its basal 10 to 14 days after establishment. There must be water in the field. If your field usually gives 3 to 4 tons, follow the lighter PhilRice plan.
Fertilizer computation for one hectare
Here is a worked fertilizer calculation for the 5 to 6 ton plan. It uses the FPA national average prices for September 14 to 18, 2026, and prices change every week.

items.title: Read the grade
items.text: Each number is a percent. A 50 kg bag of fertilizer 14 14 14 holds 7 kg each of nitrogen, phosphate and potash. A bag of urea holds 23 kg of nitrogen. Half a bag of 0 0 60 holds 15 kg of potash.

items.title: Add up the nutrients
items.text: Two bags of complete and two of urea give 14 plus 46, or 60 kg of nitrogen. They also give 14 kg of phosphate. Potash comes to 14 plus 15, or 29 kg per hectare.

items.title: Price it
items.text: Two bags of complete cost PHP 3,805.84. Two bags of urea cost PHP 4,641.38, and half a bag of potash PHP 834.04. The total is PHP 9,281.26 per hectare.

items.title: Scale it to your lot
items.text: For a 0.6 hectare lot, multiply every amount by 0.6. That is 1.2 bags of complete, 1.2 bags of urea and 15 kg of potash. The cost comes to about PHP 5,568.76.

blocks.text:
For a nutrient target, the fertilizer calculation formula is to divide the kilos of nutrient you need by the percent in the grade. Our guide to [fertilizer calculation](/blog/fertilizer-calculation) shows each step.

This plan gives less nitrogen from the bag than the general recommendation. It counts on the straw and manure for part of the rest. PhilRice says 5 tons of straw, once decomposed, can give about 30 kg of nitrogen.
Method of fertilizer application, spreaders and applicators

The method of fertilizer application matters as much as the amount. For the basal dose, IRRI advises spreading evenly and mixing it into the soil just before transplanting or seeding. In a puddled field, do it during the last harrowing. In dry direct seeding, the basal can go in through the seed drill.

For each top dressing, spread the nitrogen fertilizer evenly across the whole paddy. Then keep the bunds and outlets closed so the dissolved nutrients stay in your field. Our page on [fertilizer application methods](/blog/fertilizer-application-methods) compares broadcasting, banding and more.
Using a fertilizer spreader or applicator

On big lots, hand broadcasting rarely stays even. A hand cranked or knapsack fertilizer spreader throws granules in an even arc and saves time. A fertilizer applicator on a seed drill puts the basal dose in the rows with the seed.

Check the rate of any tool before you start. Weigh what you load, spread it over a measured area, then weigh what is left. If it drops too much or too little, adjust the opening or your walking speed.

blocks.text: Questions about fertilizer for rice

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for rice?
items.a: There is no single best fertilizer for rice. PhilRice plans use 14 14 14 or 16 20 0 at basal and urea for top dressing. Muriate of potash goes on near panicle initiation. Adjust the amounts with a soil test, MOET or the Rice Crop Manager.

items.q: How many bags of fertilizer do I need per hectare of palay?
items.a: For 5 to 6 tons, PhilRice uses 2 bags of complete or 16 20 0 and 2 bags of urea. It adds half a bag of 0 0 60, plus straw and manure.

items.q: When is the last fertilizer application for rice?
items.a: Around panicle initiation. PalayCheck puts the last nitrogen and potassium dose 5 to 7 days before or after it.
It is the rice crop management system of PhilRice, with key checks from seed to harvest. Key Check 5 covers nutrients.

items.q: Can I use ammonium sulfate instead of urea?
items.a: Yes. Use about 2.2 bags of ammonium sulfate for each bag of urea to get the same nitrogen, plus sulfur.
